Welcome to Culture of Caring, the third session of the Digital Conversion: Every Child, Every Day course. This session should take you approximately 75 minutes to complete.

You’ll need your Participant Workbook and your copy of Every Child, Every Day: A Digital Conversion Model for Student Achievement. Go ahead and pause the video while you get these resources. Click Play when you are ready to continue.

Before you begin, let’s review what you have learned in Session 2.

You looked at a definition of moral imperative.

You learned about the need for diversity of approaches, techniques, and teaching strategies for student learning.

You gained an understanding of the beliefs and expectations that lead to success.

And finally, you learned about the relationship between high expectations and the moral imperative for digital conversion.

If you want to review the entire session, you can access Session 2 on Pearson LearningStudio.

Now, take a look at the Session 2 Objectives.

During this session, you will

·implement the instructional components of a Curriculum Unit for optimal student learning and mathematical proficiency; and

·utilize Investigations resources in your classroom to personalize and differentiate instruction for your students.

By now, you should have examined the contents in your Core Curriculum Package. During this session, you will explore these components in greater depth and learn how to use specific differentiation resources in your instruction to target your students’ learning needs.

Now, watch a video that summarizes the organization of an Investigations Curriculum Unit.

In the prior sessions, you learned that a digital conversion means much more than providing technology to students. You heard about Project RED, which found that for schools to have great success, they must embrace these nine key implementation factors:

·Technology integrated into every intervention class

·Change management leadership by the principal
·Online collaboration
·Technology integrated into core subjects one or more times a week
·Online formative assessments
·One-to-one computer to student ratio
·Frequent virtual fieldtrips
·Daily use of search engines and
·Principal training


In Session 1, you participated in an activity in which you investigated the digital conversion critical success factors of Mooresville Graded School District.

One of those critical success factors was a culture of caring, which is the primary focus of this session. In the words of Dr. Mark Edwards, “I strongly believe that digital conversion cannot succeed without a pervasive culture of caring.”

In the Mooresville Graded School District, a culture of caring was central to success with the digital conversion. Therefore, it is important to have a strong understanding of what it looks like, sounds like, and feels like to be engaged in a digital conversion initiative that is going well versus one that isn’t.

A pervasive culture of caring is really a convergence of forces that create the conditions for a successful digital conversion initiative. At the heart of a digital conversion must be a commitment by everyone to the moral imperative of the conversion, which is a belief that all students can learn.

·The following factors create a culture of caring for every child and every adult:
·A commitment to every individual
·Committed leadership at all levels
·Communication of caring expectations in meetings and professional goals
·Ongoing appreciation of individuals and teams
·Professional development on how to care for students
·Involvement of every employee in the mission of learning
·Management of negative elements
·Participatory decision making at all levels to ensure buy-in and
·Laughter and fun as cultural norms


In Mooresville Graded School District, these factors came together to create an environment that was conducive to learning for all members of the community.

Watch the two videos to listen to Carol Carroll and Dr. Mark Edwards discussing the leadership roles and the “all in” attitude at Mooresville Graded School District.

After watching the videos, you will be asked to respond in your Participant Workbook.

Click the Play button on each video to watch the interviews. Once you’ve watched both videos, click Next to continue.

Answer the following questions in your Participant Workbook:

·In what ways can teachers be leaders in their schools? List specific leadership actions.

·In what ways might leaders at different levels work together?

·How might leaders at different levels engage others in participatory decision making?


When you are ready, click Next to continue.

Before continuing, please respond to the Session 3 Pause and Reflect questions in the Participant Workbook.

When you are ready, click Next to continue.

Watch the video of three principals from Mooresville Graded School District discussing how they encouraged a culture of caring among their teachers and students.

After watching the video, you will answer questions in your Participant Workbook.

Click Next to continue.

Now, answer the following questions in your Participant Workbook.

·How might district and school members celebrate new and veteran teachers who embrace change?

·How can district and school members encourage teachers to plan and support one another?

·What strategies can district and school members use to support teachers who are resistant to change?


When you are ready, click Next to continue.

Now watch a video in which two teachers discuss the culture of caring from their perspectives.

Following the video, you will again be asked to answer questions in your Participant Workbook.

Click Next to continue.

Please answer the following questions in your Participant Workbook:

·In what ways might support staff and other school personnel be engaged and recognized as part of your digital conversion initiative?

·How will parents know that their children’s teachers care about them and have high expectations for their learning?

·In what ways might parents and community members contribute to a school or district’s culture of caring?


When you are ready, click Next to continue.

Now, you’ll have a chance to watch a video of Chris Gammon, a seventh-grade social studies teacher, as he interacts with his students.

After watching the video, you will be asked to respond to the reflection questions in your Participant Workbook.
Click Next to continue.

Answer the following video reflection questions in your Participant Workbook:

·What are some ways that teachers and administrators can show that they are committed to every student?

·What strategies can teachers and administrators use to communicate to students that they care about them?



When you are ready to continue, click Next.

You’ve learned about the importance of creating a culture in your classroom, school, or district. In addition, you’ve seen how one teacher created that culture in his classroom. In the following video, you’ll see strategies for how to create a positive classroom environment.

Click Play to watch the video. Click Next to continue.

Respond to the following question in your Participant Workbook:

How can you use or adjust the strategies in this video in your own classroom, school, or district?

When you are ready to continue, click Next.

It’s time to share your thoughts with your peers! Go to the Discussion Board, and respond to the Session 3 Discussion Board questions as you reflect on the culture of caring necessary for a successful digital conversion.


When you are ready to continue, click Next.

Let’s review the objectives for this session.

·Describe the conditions necessary for a pervasive culture of caring.

·Describe the strategies teachers and leaders use to foster a culture of caring.


Now, let’s review what you have learned in this session.

You began by learning about the need for a culture of caring for a successful digital conversion initiative. Then, you learned about some of the characteristics of when a digital conversion goes well versus what it looks like when a digital conversion does not go well.

You also learned about the cultural conditions for caring. You looked at specific conditions of the culture in Mooresville Graded School District.

Next, you watched several videos on the culture of caring and how the district created that culture.

Finally, you watched a video of a teacher creating a supportive classroom environment.

In the next session, you’ll learn about data-driven decision making and how to use effective data-analysis activities to increase student achievement.

Be sure to complete the following tasks before beginning self-paced Session 4:

·Read Chapter 5 and Chapter 7 in Every Child, Every Day: A Digital Conversion Model for Student Achievement. Complete the Culture of Caring Strategies activity in your Participant Workbook.

·Apply the knowledge gained from this session to your role in the school or district before completing the next session. Record your experience in your Participant Workbook.

·Answer the Discussion Board questions, and respond to two other participants’ posts.

Now, show what you know. Visit the course home page to take the assessment for Session 3.

See you again in Session 4!
